channel.title: Ipseological Analyses
channel.description: An autonomous, reproducible analysis of Ipseity Daily data.

item.title: The 20 signifiers most diagnostic of a Republican Yes or No
item.description: In the Ipseity Daily survey, conservative was the self-description that best distinguished Yes from No on the question of whether Republican described someone that day. After comparing people surveyed on the same dates, 92.0% of the Republican Yes group endorsed conservative, compared with 11.5% of the Republican No…

item.title: What goes with calling yourself a movie lover?
item.description: The clearest clue that someone called themselves a movie lover in Ipseity Daily was that they also called themselves a film lover. After balancing the survey dates, 94.0% of the movie-lover Yes group said Yes to “film lover,” compared with 3.8% of the No group. The overlap makes sense for near synonyms. Seeing both…

item.title: Did longer survey sessions have a higher share of Yes answers?
item.description: Ipseity Daily asks adults whether words or phrases such as “trusting” describe them today. Do people who take longer to finish say Yes more often? item.title: Which signifiers best distinguish smoker Yes from No?
item.description: Which words best distinguish people who say smoker describes them today from people who answer No? In Ipseity Daily, the widest gap was for gamer. On a common mix of survey dates, 63.9% of the smoker Yes group said gamer fit them, compared with 44.8% of the smoker No group. The estimated gap was 19.0 percentage…

item.title: Which self-descriptions stayed stable across repeat surveys?
item.description: Among the most frequently repeated self-descriptions in Ipseity Daily, male had the steadiest answers. It drew the same answer on every observed date for 99.1% of repeat respondents who answered that item. Cleveland Browns fan and American followed at 96.8% and 96.2% stable. item.title: The signifiers that distinguish Democrat Yes from No
item.description: Liberal was the strongest clue that an Ipseity Daily respondent said Yes to Democrat. When the two groups were compared on the same survey dates, 91% of the Democrat Yes group said liberal described them, compared with 13% of the Democrat No group. item.title: The Ten Largest Male–Female Endorsement Gaps
